payload.answerText:
The search frame needs reshaping. The confirmed product map has five top-level regions, not eight:

**Heart of the product (two innovations):**
- Library — company knowledge made atomic and accessible to agents.
- Playbook — work processes made atomic and accessible to agents.

**Three enabling systems at the same level:**
- Viewer (was "Product Shell") — makes the system real and usable to a human director.
- Ledger — coordination and QA; the record of what has happened.
- Triggers (was "Session Wake") — activates and coordinates colleagues within the organization.

**Removed from the product map:**
- Vision Onboarding — not a product region; it is one play among what will be thousands. It is built out because it tested play capabilities.
- Knowledge Production — prototyping work in progress, not a shipped product region yet. The current exercise (this library build) is the first real knowledge-production work.

**To sort out separately:**
- Canvas — the director is unclear what the scan pulled. At least two meanings exist: the main viewer as an interactive canvas, and a very recent QA canvas concept. Needs its own conversation.

**Naming correction:**
- "Session Wake" is renamed to "Triggers" as the product name for the system that fires plays or moves within plays.

"Living business plan" is not a formal noun in the system — no card. It describes what happens when all three planes (strategy, product, learning) are connected and updating with each other. The Library itself is the card; "living business plan" is prose for what it becomes when the planes are talking.

Additional rulings from the director on the Library section:

- "Product Card" should be renamed to "Cards" — product-plane cards are just the first build; future plays will produce cards for strategy and learning planes too.
- Planes (strategy, product, learning) confirmed as correct.
- The machinery items (Thread, Section, Walk Turn, Bundle Patch, Draft Overlay, Confirmation Gate, Catalog Schema Mode) look right to the director pending definitions, not contested.
- Three plays are being developed independently — the four-question play, back of house, and front of house — and will compound into a "Start Library Build" play when proven.
- Federation is planned but unrealized. The vision: multiple libraries managed by business units (marketing, sales, finance, operations) that link to each other, creating a library of libraries. Not shipped machinery yet.

Federation is planned product machinery, not yet realized. Today each project has one library root and no federation mechanism — the PMS pointer card is the only cross-library link.

The vision: multiple libraries managed by business units (marketing, sales, finance, operations, etc.) that link to each other, creating a library of libraries — a giant company library. Federation will mean libraries "talk to" each other through links. Not shipped yet; the current build is proving the single-library path first.

The Playmaker's Studio Library pointer card is correct as a reference to the federated library that exists by director ruling, not by product machinery.

"Operating plane / mission control" is positioning prose for what Alexandria is, not a product noun. No card.

The director clarified the product's job to be done during this item: an AI colleague executes on a task or project as independently as a human peer would. Human peers are wise to have check-ins with their bosses sometimes; sometimes it's better that they just execute entirely independently. The goal is an AI colleague that fits the rhythm and culture of a director's workflows.

The index card needs revision to reflect this JTBD. The coin (the spatial representation of an agent/colleague) is the payoff to the whole system — everything else (library, playbook, ledger, triggers) exists to make that coin work. AI Colleagues may be a missing major concept in the product map. Raven is the one built-out example. These are structural observations for the index revision, not items to resolve in this walk.

Not a conflict — two complementary layers of the same system.

Atomic card categories (10 buckets: Rationale, Research, Roles, Domains, Surfaces, Entities, Capabilities, Mechanisms, Patterns, Economy) are the superstructure — the universal buckets that most product companies' nouns land in, regardless of the specific product. This is Alexandria's meta-schema for product libraries.

Product card v1 is the format each card follows once filed into one of those buckets — carrying a type (which category), a name, plane (strategy/product/learning), status (stub through confirmed), confidence, and links to other cards.

Legacy mode in the catalog schema is backward compatibility with the old 208-card quarantined library, kept for QA and comparison but not part of this process.

No card changes needed. The hot spot is resolved: categories are the superstructure, product card is the format. Two layers, one system.

Unresolved — carry as a residual gap. Triggers are the least documented and least implemented part of the system, and the domain knowledge lives largely with the director's cofounder. The current two derived-on-read trigger kinds are what's shipped, but the bigger trigger surface is not cut — it's underspecified. This library build will have gaps in the Triggers section by necessity.
Confirmed: demote Idempotency Key from a standalone card to a source-evidence note on the Ledger Event card. The director does not recognize it as a product noun — it is engineering plumbing.
Confirmed: demote State Store from a standalone card to a source-evidence note on the Ledger card. The director does not recognize it as a product noun — it is engineering plumbing.

The three-way carve is real but none of them is just "Library" unqualified:

1. The old 208-card library — a legacy artifact being kept temporarily for QA/comparison against this build. Will be retired once this library is settled.

2. What we're building now — Alexandria's initial Product Library (the 0.1 product library build for the company Alexandria). Not "a card" — it's the library itself.

3. The Playmaker's Studio Library — a separate, supporting product that will be spun out. It has its own product library because it's an independent product, even though it works with Alexandria. Companies with multiple products should have separate product libraries for each.

All three are forms of libraries, but they should each be qualified by what they are. The polysemy is real and resolved by naming: the old library goes away, this build is the Alexandria Product Library, and PMS is a separate product's library.

The Play Run is the right unit of work. The whole system exists so a director can assign a task or project to an AI colleague the same way they would to a human peer — and the way you do that is by running a play. The Play Run is what advances; the Ledger Event records what happened during that advance, and the Library is the knowledge the colleague draws on. Both serve the play run, not the other way around.

"The play" means the play definition — the playbook entry that says what this play is, what agent owns it, what it does. The Workflow Package (the runnable workflow template) and the Play Skill (the agent-facing skill file) are components of a play and should keep their own separate cards. Three artifacts, one noun, two subordinate parts.
Confirmed: demote Run Labels from a standalone card to a source-evidence note on the Play Run card. The director does not recognize it as a product noun — it is plumbing.

A Play is a definition that lives in the playbook. It is assigned to an agent and gets called by the director or by a trigger. A play includes moves — and sometimes other plays, making it a compound. Moves can be made by agents, software, or humans. The play's production lifecycle (authoring, testing, promotion) happens in Playmaker Studio, not in the shipped product. In the shipped product, a play is a bounded definition that play runs are scoped to — confirmed as context altitude.

Confirmed: the Playbook is the registry, not the page. A company has plays divided up by role; agents fill role seats and get access to plays. The /playbook page in the viewer is a derived view of the playbook-as-registry.

Confirmed: the boundary is correct. Fabro-as-orchestrator (the embedded engine that runs plays, manages gates, resumes on answers) belongs in this product library. Fabro-as-factory (the software factory that builds this repository) does not.

Five is the current intent — up to 5 direct reports for a director, each with a coin. Eventually Alexandria will support hundreds of AI colleagues, but the current model is 5 coined slots.

- Raven: the one somewhat built-out example.
- Damien: has a coin and a few off-playbook skills with stories captured in the playbook, but not truly built out.
- William: planned as the interface for Playmaker Studio. Not built yet.
- Two remaining slots: unnamed, unbuilt.

William should be carded as a planned agent. The marketing is not stale — five is the current design intent for direct reports. The distinction between "coined" (has a slot) and "built" (has real plays and capabilities) is worth noting.

Class rule for Role cards:

- Director: headline-level (pillar). The human running the show that all AI colleagues report to.
- Agent: the generic term for AI colleague. Headline-level as a concept — AI colleagues are the whole point of the system. (May need renaming to "AI Colleague" or similar if "agent" is too generic/technical.)
- Raven, Damien: instances/examples of the Agent class, not individually headline-level. They are example AI colleagues — Raven being the one somewhat built out, Damien having a coin and a few off-playbook skills.

The distinction: Director and the AI Colleague concept are pillars. Individual named agents are instances of the class, not separate pillars.

Unresolved — carry as a residual gap. The director needs to discuss with cofounder (Jess) whether code or README is canon and whether the README should be corrected. The scan's assumption (code is canon) is provisional until confirmed.

Unresolved — carry as a residual gap. The director does not recognize "Project" as a familiar product noun in this context. Needs investigation into how it's being used in the data model before a ruling can be made.

Coin is a Component, not a Surface. The Surface is the Tray — the persistent, expandable/contractable visual area for coordinating and managing AI colleagues, present across the whole viewer. Coins are components inside the Tray, each representing one AI colleague and serving as the navigation hub to that colleague's hotplays, playbook, knowledge bank, and agent page.

The Tray is a missing card — it was not found by the scan but belongs in the library. Its intent is a visual area to coordinate and manage AI colleagues. The current coin-based design is what's being tested; the Tray may not always use coins. The Tray deserves its own card as a Surface in the Viewer section. How it's represented (or not) in the current data model needs investigation.

Keep as a card for now. The director does not have enough context on this part of the system (Triggers) to rule on it. Triggers domain knowledge lives largely with the cofounder. Leave the Cursor card in place; revisit when the Triggers section gets more attention.
Keep as-is (Capability) for now. The director does not have enough context on the Triggers section to rule. Revisit when Triggers gets more attention with the cofounder.

Unresolved — carry as a residual gap. "Basic Product Description" is the current director-facing name (was "Vision," originally 9 questions boiled down to 4). The internal code still uses the old "vision" naming throughout (raven.vision.* events, /raven/vision route) because too many things were linked to it to rename safely. Needs a code cleanup when things are stable. Keep "Basic Product Description" as the card name for now since that's the outward-facing name.

One noun, two states — not two cards. Source of Truth is the objective/subjective reality the cards will be based on, gathered from the director. "Frozen" is a state of the Source of Truth (locked down so it doesn't change during atomization), not a separate thing.

Naming correction: "Raven Source of Truth" is too agent-specific. The Source of Truth should be contextualized by the move or play it's associated with, not the agent. Merge into one card named "Source of Truth" with frozen as a state, and context it by play/move rather than by agent.
Confirmed: Vision Slot is a component — one of four fixed pieces of the Basic Product Description. Not an aggregate with its own lifecycle.

payload.question: You call the libraries "a living business plan for humans" — is that a real product noun (a view over the library) that deserves a card, or prose? The nearest shipped structure is the strategy/product/learning planes.
payload.reason: Prior vocabulary lead (basis: The Work names the federated context libraries as "a living business plan for humans") with no shipped noun; nearest source structures are the knowledge-subject bands in raven-vision.ts and the matching library planes in library-catalog.ts. An inference to confirm, not a source finding.
payload.sourceResolution: No card: "living business plan" is prose for what happens when the three planes are connected and updating with each other. Same ruling renamed Product Card to Cards and confirmed the planes.

payload.question: You position the product as an "operating plane / mission control for agentic companies" — does that category deserve a card, and where would it live? The closest shipped thing is the viewer home surface with the agent coins.
payload.reason: Prior category lead (basis: The Work — "we've referred to it as an operating plane, or mission control, for agentic companies") with no shipped noun. An inference to confirm, not a source finding.
payload.sourceResolution: No card: "operating plane / mission control" is positioning prose. The ruling supplied the JTBD (an AI colleague executes as independently as a human peer would) and surfaced AI Colleague as a missing headline concept — carded in this bundle and woven into the keystone.

payload.question: You describe "a federated set of context libraries," and the PMS library does federate by ruling — but scanned source shows one library root per project and no federation mechanism. Is federation planned product machinery, or organizational practice for now?
payload.reason: Prior vocabulary lead (basis: The Work opens with "a federated set of context libraries") that source could not confirm mechanically: federation exists as a director ruling recorded as structure (the PMS pointer card), not as product machinery. An inference to confirm.
payload.sourceResolution: Federation is planned product machinery, not yet realized: business-unit libraries linking into a library of libraries. The PMS pointer card is correct as a federation-by-ruling reference.

payload.basis: every type: Concept card in this bundle (Knowledge Organization's self-referential system cards plus the pre-existing whole-product/plane keystones) is an identity-bearing structural noun, not framework drift; Entity is the closest of the ten buckets (cardType is singular in atomic-card-categories.ts; the plural 'Entities' is only the category's display label and never resolves)

payload.question: The bundle's spine treats the Play Run as the unit of work everything else advances. Is that right — or is the true unit the Ledger Event itself, or the Library? Both alternates are carded so you can re-point without a re-carve.
payload.reason: Source shows several status-carrying piles, not one: Play Run (submitted/succeeded/failed), Vision Onboarding, Knowledge Bank Area, Source Conversion, and the Library card/draft. Play Run was picked because the plays contract is the declared organizing principle and every other pile is advanced by play runs — a judgment call, not a source fact.
payload.sourceResolution: Play Run confirmed as the unit of work; the Ledger Event records what happened during an advance and the Library is the knowledge drawn on — both serve the play run.

payload.question: "Play" names three artifacts under one id — the playbook definition, the runnable workflow template, and the Raven-facing skill. When you say "the play," which one do you mean — and should the other two keep separate cards?
payload.reason: One play id covers three shipped artifacts: the Play/PLAY_MANIFEST definition, the workflows/<id>/ machine template, and the skills/<id>/SKILL.md wrapper. All three are drafted and related_to-linked; the primary is not decided here.
payload.sourceResolution: "The play" means the play definition; Workflow Package and Play Skill are its components and keep their own cards. Three artifacts, one noun, two subordinate parts.

payload.question: The product story presents triggers as first-class programmatic conditions that fire plays; shipped code has exactly two kinds, derived on read and never materialized. Is the bigger trigger surface planned, cut, or is the derived-on-read pair the intended model?
payload.reason: The design noun ("programmatic conditions which trigger a play") is bigger than the shipped runtime: triggers.ts derives only inbox.source.pending and ruling.capture.pending from ledger events on read; nothing is stored.
payload.sourceResolution: Ruled unresolved and carried as a residual gap (event d8ace377): triggers are underspecified, the domain knowledge lives with the cofounder, and the bigger surface is not cut. The Triggers section carries gaps by necessity.

payload.question: The viewer README says "/" is the only route while the code ships twelve-plus. The scan treated code as canon — confirm, and should the README be corrected?
payload.reason: packages/viewer/README.md claims a single route; viewer-routes.ts ships /playbook, /ledger, /info, /studio, /raven/vision, /raven/knowledge-bank, /agents/:id, and five library modes. Code canon, README stale.
payload.sourceResolution: Deferred and carried as a residual gap (event cc8b3b7e): whether code or README is canon needs a conversation with the cofounder; the code-is-canon assumption stays provisional.

payload.question: Two card taxonomies coexist in shipped code — the 10-folder atomic-card categories and the product-card.v1 contract (with an explicit legacy mode). Which vocabulary is the library's future, and what happens to cards in the other one?
payload.reason: atomic-card-categories.ts ships a 10-folder taxonomy while library-catalog.ts ships product-card.v1 with its own type/altitude/links contract plus an explicit legacy schema mode. Both carded and related_to-linked; never merged here.
payload.sourceResolution: Premise (a conflict to pick a winner in) overturned — recorded as a framing miss: the two taxonomies are complementary layers of one system. Categories are the superstructure (the ten universal buckets), product-card.v1 is the format; legacy mode is backward compatibility with the old 208-card library.

payload.question: The plugin markets "five specialized agents"; two ship built-in (Raven, Damien) and a third id (william) exists un-rostered. Is five the intent with three unbuilt, is the marketing stale, and should william be carded?
payload.reason: plugin.json says "Five specialized agents"; agents.ts BUILT_IN_AGENTS has two (Raven, Damien); plays.ts:7 names a william agent id with no roster entry. William is evidence inside this thread, not a card.
payload.sourceResolution: Five coined direct-report slots is the current design intent (eventually hundreds). Raven somewhat built, Damien coined with a few skills, William planned for PMS and now carded, two slots unnamed. Coined-vs-built distinction noted on the Agent card.

payload.question: Fabro wears two hats — the shipped embedded orchestrator inside the product and the software factory that builds this repository. The carve kept only the shipped hat in scope; confirm that boundary is the right one for the library.
payload.reason: orchestration.ts is the in-scope shipped orchestrator; the factory that builds the repo is out of scope per the manifest. Flagged so downstream carving never merges the two roles.
payload.sourceResolution: Boundary confirmed: the shipped embedded orchestrator belongs in this library; the software factory that builds the repo does not.

payload.question: "Library" means three things: the pre-convention 208-card legacy library (held back as an oracle, not carded), the product-card.v1 catalog (the Library card), and the federated PMS library (a pointer card). Is that three-way carve right?
payload.reason: The legacy 208-card library is an excluded oracle per the manifest; the product-card.v1 catalog is carded as Entity - Library; the PMS library federates as a Reference pointer. Proposed carve, director ratifies.
payload.sourceResolution: Three-way carve confirmed with qualified names: the old 208-card library retires once this build settles; this build is the Alexandria Product Library (card renamed accordingly); the PMS library belongs to a separate product.

payload.question: Is the coin a Surface (the place you meet and fire an agent) or a Component (a rendering inside the agents surface)? It is drafted provisionally as Surface — pick.
payload.reason: The pass1 resolution (the coin is the agent's rendering, not a distinct place) is exactly what makes its category ambiguous between Surface and Component. Drafted provisionally as Surface; both candidates named.
payload.sourceResolution: Coin is a Component (card retyped) — the provisional Surface drafting was a miss. The Surface is the Tray, which the scan missed entirely; Surface - Tray added by this ruling.

payload.question: "Source of Truth" means two things — the Raven Vision prose kept current as slots resolve, and the conversion output you freeze for atomization. Keep the split into two cards, or rule them one noun with two states?
payload.reason: Two lifecycles, owners, and consumers share a folder family and a name: RavenSourceOfTruthState (current, content-hashed, flushed from slots) vs source_of_truth.frozen (the atomization input). Both cards drafted and related_to-linked.
payload.sourceResolution: The proposed split was overruled: one noun, two states — frozen is a state of the Source of Truth, not a separate thing. Cards merged into Entity - Source of Truth, contexted by play/move rather than agent ("Raven Source of Truth" was too agent-specific).

payload.question: Would you say "state store"? It reads as implementation machinery exposed as a noun — the walk proposes demoting it to a source-evidence note on the Ledger card. Confirm or keep.
payload.reason: State Store fails the spoken-vocabulary (UL) test: append machinery, not product language. Proposed demotion; kept as a drafted card pending the ruling, never silently deleted.
payload.sourceResolution: Demotion confirmed: engineering plumbing, now a source-evidence note on the Ledger card; the State Store card is kept deprecated as the record.

payload.question: Is "idempotency key" a product noun or plumbing? The walk proposes demoting it to a source-evidence note on Ledger Event. Confirm or keep.
payload.reason: Plumbing vocabulary — the retry-safety key on appends. Proposed demotion to a note on Entity - Ledger Event.
payload.sourceResolution: Demotion confirmed: engineering plumbing, now a source-evidence note on the Ledger Event card; the card is kept deprecated as the record.

payload.question: Is the delivery cursor worth a card, or is it wake-internals? The walk proposes demoting it to a note on Wake Subscription. Confirm or keep.
payload.reason: At-least-once delivery machinery; fails the spoken-vocabulary test outside the wake internals. Proposed demotion to a note on Entity - Wake Subscription.
payload.sourceResolution: Demotion declined for now: the director lacks context on Triggers to rule; the Cursor card stays, revisit when Triggers gets attention with the cofounder.

payload.question: playRunId / playId / projectId are line-label identifiers, not spoken product nouns. The walk proposes demoting Run Labels to a note on Play Run. Confirm or keep.
payload.reason: Line-label nouns — exactly the class the UL test exists to catch. Proposed demotion to a source-evidence note on Entity - Play Run.
payload.sourceResolution: Demotion confirmed: plumbing, now a note on the Play Run card; the Run Labels card is kept deprecated as the record.

payload.question: Is the Playbook the registry (an Entity) or the /playbook page (a Surface)? Drafted as the registry with the route as a derived view — confirm or flip.
payload.reason: The Playbook interface / PLAY_MANIFEST (registry) and the /playbook route (surface) split the Entity-vs-Surface reading. Drafted provisionally as Entity; the route treated as derived_from the registry.
payload.sourceResolution: The Playbook is the registry, not the page: plays divided by role, agents fill role seats; the /playbook route is a derived view.

payload.question: Which name is canonical — the director-facing "Basic Product Description" or the internal vision id (raven.vision.* events, /raven/vision route)? The card is drafted with the director-facing name; ratify or rename.
payload.reason: Director-facing label vs internal id/events/route disagree. prefLabel proposed as Basic Product Description with Vision / Raven Vision as altLabels; EL3 ratifies.
payload.sourceResolution: Deferred and carried as a residual gap (event 5072f3be): "Basic Product Description" stays as the director-facing card name; internal vision naming needs a code cleanup pass when things are stable.

payload.question: Is a Wake the operation of waking (Capability) or the wake-request record with its requested → delivered / failed life (Entity)? Drafted provisionally as Capability — pick.
payload.reason: The session.wake.requested/.delivered/.failed lifecycle makes an Entity reading honest; the delivery act makes Capability honest. Both candidates named.
payload.sourceResolution: Kept as Capability for now: the director deferred the type question until Triggers gets attention with the cofounder.

payload.question: Does the Project sit at context altitude (the bounded workspace everything lives in) or aggregate (initialized into a configured state)? Provisional: context — confirm.
payload.reason: Genuinely between context and aggregate: bounded like a context, but ax init carries it into a configured state like an aggregate. Provisional context; both candidates named.
payload.sourceResolution: Carried as a residual gap (event c5a12ae8): the director does not recognize "Project" as a product noun here; how the data model uses it needs investigation before a ruling.

payload.question: Where do actors sit on a thing-shaped altitude ladder? Raven and the Director read as pillars (headline parts of the product); the Role class otherwise reads as context. Set a class rule for all four Role cards.
payload.reason: C4's ladder is thing-shaped, not actor-shaped. All four Role cards carry provisional context altitude; Raven and Director arguably pillar. A class ruling is needed rather than four one-offs.
payload.sourceResolution: Class rule set: Director is a pillar; the Agent/AI Colleague concept is headline-level (Concept - AI Colleague added); named agents are instances at context altitude, not pillars.

payload.question: Does a Play sit at context altitude (a bounded definition runs are scoped to) or aggregate (identity-bearing)? In this product it has no state transitions — its production lifecycle lives in the Studio. Provisional: context — confirm.
payload.reason: PLAY_MANIFEST entries are identity-bearing but carry no in-product state transitions; the lifecycle lives in the Playmaker's Studio, not this product. Provisional context; both candidates named.
payload.sourceResolution: Context altitude confirmed: a play is a bounded definition play runs are scoped to; its production lifecycle lives in Playmaker Studio, not the shipped product.

payload.question: Is a Vision Slot a component (one of four fixed pieces of the description) or an aggregate (it carries its own needs_review → approved/skipped transitions)? Provisional: component — confirm.
payload.reason: The slot has its own status enum but no life outside the description. Provisional component; both candidates named.
payload.sourceResolution: Component confirmed: one of four fixed pieces of the Basic Product Description, no lifecycle of its own.

payload.question: We took the domain to be the shipped Alexandria product line — plugin, ax CLI, viewer, product docs — and fenced out the OS-for-chaotic-orgs category, the pile-of-skills and prompt-engineering look-alikes, plus the legacy library, the Studio (federated), vendored repos, and deploy/factory tooling. Did that search frame hold, or did the scan miss a region you consider the product?
payload.reason: Search-frame confirmation: the prior's assumed domain plus its high-confidence fence and the manifest's exclusions, surfaced for the director to confirm the scan covered the right space — not a source finding.
payload.sourceResolution: Premise overturned — recorded as a scan miss: the eight-container frame did not hold. The director ruled five top-level regions (Library and Playbook at the heart; Viewer, Ledger, Triggers enabling), removed Vision Onboarding (one play among thousands) and Knowledge Production (prototyping) from the map, renamed Session Wake to Triggers, and held Canvas for its own conversation. Enacted in this bundle. (Also recorded as event 32f5fe6b in the second run.)
